Definition: Is the register integrated with the government's national data exchange system?
Comments: RNE has policy for instant electronic data exchange (web services).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: RNE's data-exchange page (fetched) confirms only bespoke KYC/UBO web-service API contracts under a 2020 interoperability decree, with no confirmed connection to the national UXP interoperability platform, whose 2024 Phase 1 onboarded only Interior, Education, Transport and Social Affairs — not the business registry (Cybernetica; Tunisian-Estonian Chamber of Commerce). Evidence supports partial rather than full nationwide integration; downgraded from 5 to 4.

Definition: What proportion of businesses does the register cover?
Comments: ~800k registered companies; informal sector significant, estimate 50-69% formal coverage.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: INS confirms 824,593 registered private enterprises in the RNE as of end-2023 (up from ~800k in 2020), while informal-economy estimates put informality at roughly 37-45% of activity/employment (MIMIC 2020; Carnegie 2019), consistent with a 50-69% economy-wide formal coverage estimate. Note: metadata guidance suggests using total formal businesses (not the whole economy) as denominator, in which case RNE — INS's own exhaustive register of patented firms — would show near-complete coverage; this interpretive ambiguity is flagged for human review rather than resolved by a code change.

Comments: Includes all non-citizens/foreigners who have civil status in Tunisia.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: Law 57-3 (1957) mandates registration of births/deaths for any person present in Tunisia regardless of nationality, and Madania holds records for foreigners with civil status in Tunisia. No change, though UNHCR/statelessness research notes Tunisia lacks a dedicated refugee legal framework, so practical access for asylum seekers/stateless persons may be narrower than the de jure position.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original 2013 UN-GGIM source is now dead and outdated. This indicates the cadastre remains under active development rather than partially deployed; downgraded from 4 to 3.
